section: Moderate phase (1885-1905) - leaders, methods, demands and achievements; economic critique of colonialism
subsections: British Committee of INC and Indian Parliamentary Committee
Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s: The British Committee of the Indian National Congress was established in which of the following places and years?
accepted.x: The British Committee of the INC was formed in London in 1889.
accepted.tq: Use the place–year combination to distinguish the British Committee from the later Parliamentary Committee.
accepted.sec: British Committee of INC and Indian Parliamentary Committee

accepted.s: Who chaired the British Committee of the Indian National Congress?
accepted.x: William Wedderburn chaired the British Committee of the INC.
accepted.tq: Identify the office-holder directly rather than confusing the chairperson with the organisers.
accepted.sec: British Committee of INC and Indian Parliamentary Committee

accepted.s: The journal associated with the British Committee of the Indian National Congress was
accepted.x: The British Committee published the journal India, which began in 1890.
accepted.tq: Match the organisation with its specific publication.
accepted.sec: British Committee of INC and Indian Parliamentary Committee

accepted.s: The principal objective of the British Committee of the INC was to
o: carry the Indian case to the British public and Parliament
organise armed resistance in Britain against the colonial government
establish a separate Indian army in London
conduct elections to the Indian legislative councils
accepted.x: The Committee lobbied British public opinion and Parliament for Indian reforms.
accepted.tq: Ask what function the organisation performed rather than where it was located.
accepted.sec: British Committee of INC and Indian Parliamentary Committee

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the British Committee of the INC:
1. It was formed in London in 1889.
2. William Wedderburn and Dadabhai Naoroji were associated with its formation.
3. Its journal was titled India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the Committee was formed in London in 1889, was associated with Wedderburn and Naoroji, and published India.
accepted.tq: Check the date, associated persons and publication before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: British Committee of INC and Indian Parliamentary Committee

accepted.s: Which pair of persons is correctly associated with the setting up of the Indian Parliamentary Committee in 1893?
o: William Wedderburn and W. S. Caine
Dadabhai Naoroji and A. O. Hume
W. S. Caine and Lord Curzon
accepted.x: The Indian Parliamentary Committee was set up by William Wedderburn and W. S. Caine.
accepted.tq: Separate the named founders of the Parliamentary Committee from other contemporary leaders and officials.
accepted.sec: British Committee of INC and Indian Parliamentary Committee

accepted.s: Who among the following wrote the biography of A. O. Hume published in 1913?
accepted.x: William Wedderburn wrote Hume’s biography, published in 1913.
accepted.tq: Use the author–work association and avoid assigning the work to a prominent Indian Moderate.
accepted.sec: British Committee of INC and Indian Parliamentary Committee

accepted.s: William Wedderburn presided over the Indian National Congress session held at
accepted.x: William Wedderburn was President of the INC at its Bombay session in 1889.
accepted.tq: Link the leader with the correct Congress session and year.
accepted.sec: British Committee of INC and Indian Parliamentary Committee

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a constitutional demand of the Moderates?
o: Immediate establishment of a republican government
Larger councils with elected members and control over the budget
Replacement of the civil services by elected village bodies
accepted.x: The Moderates demanded larger legislative councils, elected representation and power over the budget.
accepted.tq: Identify the demand that belongs to the constitutional sphere without extending it into later extremist objectives.
accepted.sec: Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s: The Moderate demand expressed by the slogan “No Taxation Without Representation” was most directly related to
o: control over the budget by representative legislative councils
separation of the judiciary from the executive
abolition of the Indian Civil Service examination
accepted.x: The slogan referred to the demand for representative councils with power over taxation and the budget.
accepted.tq: Translate the slogan into its constitutional implication.
accepted.sec: Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s:
Which of the following was an administrative demand of the Moderates?
1. Simultaneous ICS examinations in India and England
2. Raising the age limit for the ICS examination
3. Separation of the judiciary from the executive
4. Complete abolition of the civil services
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Moderates demanded simultaneous examinations, a higher ICS age limit and separation of the judiciary from the executive. They did not demand complete abolition of the civil services.
accepted.tq: Find the extreme administrative claim that does not fit the Moderate programme.
accepted.sec: Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s: The demand for simultaneous ICS examinations in India and England was intended chiefly to promote
o: the appointment of British judges in provincial courts
accepted.x: Holding the examination in India as well as England was intended to make entry into the higher services more accessible to Indians and promote Indianisation.
accepted.tq: Connect the institutional demand with its intended administrative result.
accepted.sec: Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT an economic demand of the Moderates?
o: Expansion of military expenditure on imperial wars
accepted.x: The Moderates demanded cuts in military expenditure, particularly expenditure on imperial wars, rather than its expansion.
accepted.tq: Locate the reversed economic demand by checking the direction of the proposed change.
accepted.sec: Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s: The military expenditure that the Moderates particularly sought to reduce was expenditure on imperial wars in
accepted.x: The Moderates opposed the financial burden of imperial wars, especially those in Afghanistan and Burma.
accepted.tq: Recall the two specific theatres named in the military expenditure demand.
accepted.sec: Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s:
Consider the following demands of the Moderates:
1. Lower land revenue
2. Abolition of the salt tax
3. Tariff protection for Indian industries
4. Welfare expenditure on irrigation
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four were part of the Moderate economic programme: lower land revenue, abolition of the salt tax, tariff protection and welfare expenditure such as irrigation.
accepted.tq: Group the listed demands by recognising that the Moderates sought both tax relief and productive welfare spending.
accepted.sec: Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s: The civil-rights demands of the Moderates included freedom of
o: property, taxation and military service only
accepted.x: Freedom of speech, press and association were central civil-rights demands of the Moderates.
accepted.tq: Recall the standard three-part civil-rights demand without substituting other freedoms.
accepted.sec: Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s: The Moderate leadership protested against which combination of official actions?
o: Tilak’s arrest and the deportation of the Natu brothers without trial
Gokhale’s arrest and the exile of Dadabhai Naoroji
Curzon’s resignation and the imprisonment of Wedderburn
The closure of the British Committee and the ban on India
accepted.x: The Moderates expressed outrage at Tilak’s arrest and the deportation of the Natu brothers without trial.
accepted.tq: Match the civil-rights protest with the correct persons and official actions.
accepted.sec: Demands - councils, ICS, military expenditure, Indianisation, tax relief

accepted.s: Which of the following best represents the principal methods of the Moderate phase?
o: Secret societies, assassinations and armed insurrection
Boycott, passive resistance and mass civil disobedience
Prayers, petitions and protests through constitutional agitation
accepted.x: The Moderate method is commonly represented by the three Ps—prayers, petitions and protests—within a constitutional framework.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive three-P formulation to separate Moderate methods from later methods.
accepted.sec: Methods and limitations

accepted.s: The Moderates adopted a two-pronged strategy consisting of
o: building public opinion in India and persuading the British public and government
working only through the princely states
boycotting British goods and forming parallel governments
organising the army and securing foreign military aid
accepted.x: Their strategy combined the creation of public opinion in India with efforts to persuade British public opinion and the government.
accepted.tq: Identify both elements of the strategy rather than choosing only the domestic or British component.
accepted.sec: Methods and limitations

accepted.s: The Moderate belief that British rule was “providential” was associated with their faith in
o: the permanent supremacy of princely states
accepted.x: The Moderates believed that British rule was providential and initially placed faith in British justice and fair play.
accepted.tq: Match the ideological belief with the method it encouraged.
accepted.sec: Methods and limitations

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the working of the Indian National Congress during the Moderate phase:
1. Its annual session generally lasted only three days.
2. It had an effective permanent machinery functioning between sessions.
3. It relied on resolutions, meetings and pamphlets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The annual session lasted only about three days and the Congress used resolutions, meetings and pamphlets. It had no effective machinery to work between sessions.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the known organisational limitation of the Congress.
accepted.sec: Methods and limitations

accepted.s: A major limitation of the Moderate movement was that its social base was largely confined to
accepted.x: The Moderate movement had a narrow social base consisting largely of the urban educated elite.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the actual social base from the wider mass participation associated with later phases.
accepted.sec: Methods and limitations

accepted.s: The Moderates’ “naive faith” in British justice was most clearly exposed by the
o: establishment of the Indian Parliamentary Committee in 1893
appointment of the Welby Commission in 1895
formation of the British Committee in 1889
accepted.x: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 exposed the limitations of the Moderate faith in British justice and fair play.
accepted.tq: Use the cause-and-effect link between an official action and the weakening of Moderate faith.
accepted.sec: Methods and limitations

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT an achievement of the Moderate phase?
o: Development of a pan-Indian national identity
Training in parliamentary politics and civil liberties
accepted.x: The Moderates fostered national identity, economic critique and democratic training, but they did not achieve complete independence.
accepted.tq: Identify the later ultimate objective incorrectly projected onto the Moderate phase.
accepted.sec: Methods and limitations

accepted.s: The economic critique developed by the Moderates was later used by
o: the British Committee and the Welby Commission alone
the princely states against the Congress
accepted.x: The Moderate economic critique of colonial rule became an important intellectual resource for the Extremists and Gandhi.
accepted.tq: Trace the later influence of an ideological achievement rather than a constitutional concession.
accepted.sec: Methods and limitations

accepted.s: The statement that the Congress was “tottering to its fall” and should be assisted to a “peaceful demise” was made by
accepted.x: Lord Curzon made this remark in 1900 while expressing his hostile attitude towards the Congress.
accepted.tq: Use the speaker–year pairing to distinguish Curzon’s remark from Dufferin’s description.
accepted.sec: Official attitude to the Moderates

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Indian Councils Act of 1892?
o: It ended nomination and gave all legislative members the right to vote.
It introduced direct elections and gave councils power to amend the budget.
It abolished official majority in the councils and established responsible government.
It enlarged councils and introduced indirect election, but did not permit voting or amendment of the budget.
accepted.x: The Act enlarged the councils and introduced indirect election through nomination on the recommendation of bodies. Members could discuss the budget but could neither vote on nor amend it, and officials retained their majority.
accepted.tq: Separate enlargement and indirect election from the stronger powers that the Act did not grant.
accepted.sec: Achievements - Indian Councils Act 1892

accepted.s: Under the Indian Councils Act of 1892, members of the legislative councils could
o: reject the entire budget by majority vote
discuss the budget but not vote on or amend it
vote on and amend the budget without restriction
exercise complete control over military expenditure
accepted.x: The Act allowed discussion of the budget but denied members the right to vote on or amend it.
accepted.tq: Distinguish discussion from the more substantial powers of voting and amendment.
accepted.sec: Achievements - Indian Councils Act 1892

accepted.s: Which of the following was a feature of representation under the Indian Councils Act, 1892?
o: Direct election by universal adult franchise
Selection exclusively by the Governor-General without recommendations
Election only by members of the British Parliament
Indirect election through nomination on the recommendation of bodies
accepted.x: The Act introduced an indirect electoral principle through nomination on the recommendation of specified bodies.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact constitutional mechanism instead of substituting modern direct elections.
accepted.sec: Achievements - Indian Councils Act 1892

accepted.s:
Why did the Indian National Congress regard the Indian Councils Act of 1892 as inadequate?
1. There was no direct vote.
2. Officials retained a majority.
3. The budget could be discussed but not amended.
4. The Act abolished all legislative councils.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Congress considered the Act inadequate because it provided no direct vote, retained an official majority and denied the power to amend the budget. It did not abolish the legislative councils.
accepted.tq: Combine the three genuine grievances and reject the exaggerated abolition claim.
accepted.sec: Achievements - Indian Councils Act 1892

accepted.s: The grievance of the Congress regarding the “sham” Councils Act of 1861 was connected with the later inadequacy of the
accepted.x: The Congress’s criticism of the inadequate Indian Councils Act of 1892 was linked to its earlier grievance against the “sham” Councils Act of 1861.
accepted.tq: Connect the earlier constitutional grievance with the later Act that failed to meet Moderate demands.
accepted.sec: Achievements - Indian Councils Act 1892

accepted.s: The Welby Commission, appointed in 1895, examined
o: the working of the British Committee’s journal
the structure of the Indian Civil Service examination
accepted.x: The Welby Commission of 1895 dealt with Indian expenditure and was regarded as one of the gains associated with Moderate pressure.
accepted.tq: Match the commission with its specific subject rather than with another contemporary issue.
accepted.sec: Methods and limitations
